The DAWN-plasma trial was a phase 2, randomized, open-label, multicenter proof-of-concept study. It compared standard of care (SOC) plus convalescent plasma with SOC alone in adults hospitalized with COVID-19. Ethics committees at each center approved the study, which followed the Declaration of Helsinki and ICH GCP guidelines. Signed or witnessed verbal informed consent was required.

**Rationale and design**
- The investigators hypothesized that early, high-volume, high-titer convalescent plasma would reduce the need for mechanical ventilation.
- Patients were randomized 2:1 to plasma or control.
- The primary endpoint was the percentage of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15.
- Secondary endpoints included clinical status, mortality, ventilation, safety and quality of life.
- Patients already receiving mechanical ventilation were excluded, as were those with recent anti-CD20 therapy or prior severe plasma reactions.
- The plasma group received 4 units (800–1000 mL) in two doses. The first dose was given within 12 hours of randomization and the second 24–36 hours later. Neutralizing antibody titers had to be at least 1/160.

**Conduct**
- Between May 2, 2020 and January 26, 2021, 489 patients were randomized.
- The Full Analysis Set comprised 320 plasma and 163 control patients, after excluding one patient without confirmed SARS-CoV-2 and five who withdrew consent.
- Baseline characteristics and concomitant therapy were similar between groups.
- Median time to first transfusion was 5 hours, and median volume was 884 mL. Of the units given, 80.7% had titers of at least 1/320, and 91.9% of plasma patients received all 4 units.

**Efficacy**
- At Day 15, 83.7% of plasma patients and 84.1% of controls were alive without mechanical ventilation (OR 0.99, p=0.976).
- A significant subgroup interaction with age was found (p=0.023).
- No secondary endpoint differed significantly, and Per Protocol results were similar.
- Neutralizing antibody titers rose by Day 6 independent of the intervention. Higher titers at Day 0 and Day 6 correlated with better outcomes.

**Safety**
- Adverse events occurred in 28.13% of plasma patients and 30.06% of controls.
- Fatal adverse events occurred in 10.31% and 9.82%, respectively, and serious adverse events in about 21% of each group.
- Transfusion-related side effects occurred in 6.0% of plasma patients, with no TRALI cases.
- Laboratory parameters and body temperature were similar between groups.

**Conclusion**
Early high-volume, high-titer convalescent plasma did not change the clinical course of hospitalized COVID-19 patients.

Veteran Rodney Orton, who has used a mobility scooter for 15 years because of breathing problems, was left without one when it stopped working. The VA told him he needed a new evaluation, with the next appointment six weeks away, even though he was already admitted to a VA hospital. After Problem Solver Travis Guillory contacted the VA, Assistant Chief of Prosthetics Diana Kinion found a suitable scooter in local inventory and delivered it to his room the next morning.

This study presents a quantitative bibliometric analysis of research on STEAM education combined with gamification. The introduction cites prior research showing that gamification can enhance student motivation, engagement, and academic performance. It also notes that effects vary with individual personality factors, may diminish over time, and require further systematic study.

**Method**
- The authors searched Scopus on October 23, 2023, using the terms "steam" AND "gamification," limited to English.
- The search returned 45 documents. After filtering for 2017–2023, 35 remained, and 34 English-language documents formed the final dataset.

**Findings**
- **Publication trend:** Output began in 2017, and annual output rose from 4 to 8 documents during 2020–2023, peaking in 2022.
- **Most-cited paper:** Wannapiroon and Pimdee's 2022 study on Thai undergraduate STEAM creative thinking, with 30 citations.
- **Top source:** CEUR Workshop Proceedings had the most publications.
- **Most productive authors:** Kummanee, Lee, Nilsook, Piriyasurawong, and Wannapiroon, with three publications each.
- **Leading countries:** Thailand, Bulgaria, Italy, and Malaysia. Thailand had the most publications (6) and citations (68).
- **Collaboration:** Germany, Latvia, Norway, and France were most active in joint research, and Malaysia had the highest link strength.
- **Subject areas:** Computer science accounted for 37.7% of papers, followed by social sciences (20.5%) and engineering (16.9%).
- **Keywords:** The dominant keywords were gamification, STEAM, STEAM education, and computational thinking.
- **Factorial analysis:** Three topic clusters emerged:
  - educational methodologies and tools
  - student-centered learning environments
  - educational technologies and engagement strategies

**Conclusion**
Over seven years, the field produced 34 documents and 155 citations, and the authors expect its growth to continue.

Libyan National Army forces have lost four men, killed by snipers and a landmine, and had 10 wounded in December fighting in Benghazi's Khreibish district, months after Khalifa Haftar declared victory there.

Abercrombie & Fitch CEO Fran Horowitz, ranked No. 26 on this year's MPW list, told the Most Powerful Women summit in Washington, D.C., that the company aims to be a long-lasting lifestyle brand rather than "cool." After the brand crashed a decade ago over sexualized marketing and disdain toward shoppers, Horowitz, formerly Hollister's president, took over in 2017. She replaced command-and-control management with more employee input, raised clothing quality, and stopped chasing trends. A&F sales nearly doubled to $2.6 billion from 2019 to 2024, and combined A&F and Hollister sales will top $5 billion this year. To sustain growth, she has pursued partnerships: Abercrombie Kids now sells at Macy's, and A&F became the NFL's first fashion partner. Horowitz says this targets female fans, who make up half the fanbase and are underserved by "pink and sparkly" merchandise.

This patent application describes electronic gaming systems and methods featuring a stop-based bonus game, such as a wheel or reel with multiple stop positions. It is a continuation of earlier applications, the earliest a provisional filed September 1, 2017.

**Core mechanic:** The bonus game uses two award classes:
- **First awards:** more desirable awards, such as jackpots, which may be fixed or progressive.
- **Second awards:** lesser awards, such as small credit amounts, multipliers, wild symbols, free plays, or no-value awards.

When a player lands on a stop position tied to a second award, the player receives that award. That position is then converted to a first award for future plays. As a result, the number of jackpot positions grows with continued play, increasing the apparent chance of winning a jackpot.

**Persistence and resets:**
- These changes persist across gaming sessions, so a later player may win a jackpot added during an earlier player's session.
- When a jackpot is won, positions may reset to a default state or be reduced in number.

**Constructs:** Possible formats include wheels, reels, dice, and grid-based "treasure maps." In the grid format, players select regions themselves, and award locations may be randomized before each play while preserving their proportions.

**Example implementation:**
1. A base game outcome triggers a bonus wheel with inner and outer wheels.
2. The bonus wheel can lead to one of four secondary jackpot wheels (GRAND, MAJOR, MINOR, MINI).
3. On these wheels, credit prizes landed on are replaced with jackpot awards.

**Supporting content:** The document also describes networked EGM hardware, servers, player tracking, and regulatory considerations. It states that the invention increases player investment and sustains interest by rewarding continued play with an "upgraded" bonus game.

Santiago and Mattos describe a remote dialogic educational activity developed during the COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil. They designed it with Paulo Freire's critical pedagogy and analyzed it through Cultural-Historical Activity Theory (CHAT). The pandemic forced schools into emergency remote teaching and deepened socioeconomic inequality in Brazil, where the government denied science as the proper response to the health crisis.

**Theoretical framework**
- **CHAT:** Drawing on Leontyev and Engeström, the authors treat educational activity as a complex system. In it, subjects, objects and community are mediated by tools, rules and the division of labor, and contradictions drive change.
- **Dialogue:** They treat dialogue as an activity, not merely an exchange of ideas. Following Freire, it rests on love, humility, faith, trust, hope and critical thinking.
- **Aim:** The activity sought to increase students' conscious awareness of the contradictions they live.

**The activity**
- **Setting:** The activity took place on Discord, a gaming platform familiar to many students. It ran in a "Non-Formal Education" course for 19 physics teacher education students at a Brazilian federal university.
- **Platform setup:** The teacher created text and voice channels. Students could join any group at any time without teacher management.
- **Design:** The activity had seven stages. The teacher hypothesized the theme, the tension over reopening schools, and connected it to science communication content.
- **Process:** Students discussed their pandemic difficulties, such as time management, household burdens and lack of in-person interaction. They then debated school reopening, researched reliable sources, and produced an infographic on the pros and cons of returning to in-person classes. They shared it mainly via WhatsApp, but its reach could not be measured.

**Findings**
- Discord enabled students to self-organize, move between groups, and hold meetings without the teacher.
- Students divided tasks based on their technological abilities, increasing their agency and creating a new division of labor.
- Some students moved from text to voice as topics became more meaningful, overcoming the inhibition some experience in face-to-face classes.

**Key factors in the outcome**
- Students' prior familiarity with Discord.
- Freirean thematic organization rooted in students' own problems.
- Collective production linking students' individual problems to broader socio-political issues.

The authors note that participants had better internet access than most Brazilian public education students. They conclude that the activity fostered autonomy, student voice, and awareness that school reopening is a collective socio-political problem rather than only an individual one.
For some dogs, an irresistible attraction to toys may parallel human behavioral addictions.

A Stanford University psychology study tested whether descriptive vegetable labels would lead college students to eat more vegetables. Identically prepared dishes were labeled in one of four ways: indulgent, basic, healthy-restrictive, or healthy-positive. Among nearly 28,000 students, indulgent labels led diners to choose vegetables 25 percent more often than basic labels, 35 percent more often than healthy-positive labels, and 41 percent more often than healthy-restrictive labels. Students also took larger portions.

The author notes that taste drives food choices more broadly. Campbell's restored sodium to its soups after reduced-salt versions sold poorly. A 2017 IFIC survey found that 84 percent of respondents cite taste as a key purchase driver, compared with 63 percent who cite healthfulness. Only about 10 percent of American adults and 1 percent of teens and tweens meet vegetable recommendations.

The author suggests applying this approach at home and recommends appealing-sounding recipes:
- Grilled carrot fries with chipotle lime aioli
- Nacho cheese kale chips
- Chili lime sweet corn salad
- Rosemary sea salt and vinegar beet chips
- Cauliflower fried rice
- Sautéed green beans with bleu cheese and walnuts

NASA shared a Hubble Space Telescope image of the Tarantula Nebula (30 Doradus), named for its spidery gas filaments. It also shows the bubble-shaped Honeycomb Nebula, whose appearance 2010 research links to two interacting supernovae and our viewing angle.

This lecture segment covers electroweak unification, the combination of the weak and electromagnetic interactions. Two issues arise. First, the interactions differ greatly in strength, which heavy gauge bosons acting as mediators may account for. Second, their coupling structures differ: QED uses vector coupling, while the weak interaction uses vector-axial (1 minus gamma 5) coupling. The lecturer addresses the second issue by absorbing the 1 minus gamma 5 term into the spinor definitions, projecting out left-handed components. The weak current then becomes a vector current. The electromagnetic current splits into separate left- and right-handed parts with no mixed term, which explains why QED does not change helicity.

Using concepts from strong isospin, the neutrino and electron are written as a doublet. Charged weak currents are expressed with tau-plus and tau-minus matrices, and the third component resembles a neutral current. By analogy with the Gell-Mann-Nishijima equation, a hypercharge current is defined. It includes right-handed particles, which the neutral current previously lacked. This is generalized to all particle doublets, with the caveat that mass eigenstates differ from weak eigenstates.

An isospin triplet (W1, W2, W3) and a hypercharge singlet (B) are introduced. W-plus and W-minus are combinations of W1 and W2. The photon and Z boson arise from mixing W3 and B through the weak mixing angle theta W, with the couplings related to the electromagnetic coupling. This yields a consistent picture unifying the two interactions.

In a December 11, 2017 article, Harry Slater offers five tips for Asmodee Digital's new digital version of the board game Abalone, which features updated graphics and other tweaks:

1. **Don't rush in:** Attacking immediately leaves you vulnerable.
2. **Plan ahead:** As in chess, anticipate the board, avoid weaknesses in your lines, and exploit opponent mistakes.
3. **Get to the centre:** Central control increases mobility and reaction speed.
4. **Go on the offensive eventually:** The first player to remove five opposing counters is in pole position to win.
5. **Split them up:** Divide opposing counters, push groups toward the edge, and watch for counterattacks.

This March 2006 AMD specification update (31534D) lists silicon errata for the AMD Geode™ CS5535 Companion Device, Revision A3. Issue numbers are not sequential because resolved issues are omitted. Each entry gives a description, implications, and a resolution where one exists.

**Timers, interrupts, and DMA**
- The PIT does not let a read-back command cancel a pending latch command.
- PIT count mode 3 loads new count values immediately.
- The XPIC delays clearing the IRR bit, causing duplicate interrupts under AEOI.
- PIC edge-triggered inputs can miss interrupts, and potentially hang the system, when Local bus clock gating is enabled.
- PIC Polling mode is unsupported.
- DMA rotating priority does not rotate correctly.
- UARTs and LPC devices cannot be reliably accessed during block or demand mode legacy DMA. Single transfer mode is recommended instead.

**IDE/ATAC**
- UDMA write CRC errors can follow a UDMA read with host termination. The workaround is the I/O blocking feature in the ATAC Error MSR.
- The ATAC can hang with non-DWORD-aligned PRDs.
- UDMA fails if the bus master is enabled before the PIO command packet is sent.
- A device interrupt resets the bus master engine.
- The SSMI-during-DMA feature does not block I/O.
- tACK settings have no effect on timing.

**Power management**
- Byte accesses to PM1_STS and PM1_EN hang the system.
- WORD and BYTE writes to PMC registers can corrupt other register writes.
- Most wake inputs fail from ACPI S3, so PWRBTN# with external circuitry should be used.
- LOWBAT_FLAG is not set after abnormal standby.
- SLEEP_X/SLEEP_Y fail to deassert unless their delays are less than PM_SED.
- The Sleep Clock option must be enabled in the PMC whenever other sleep options are used.
- Recovery from a thermal-alarm Faulted Standby repeats until the alarm clears.

**Clock gating**
Automatic clock gating fails in three cases, and the resolution is to disable it:
- The UART domain in CEIR mode
- The USB controllers
- The main GLIU domain for statistics-counter ASMIs

**Bus and interface issues**
- I/O addresses at 10000h or higher hang the system, and LBARs permit such illegal values.
- USB over-voltage protection does not meet USB 1.1, so external protection is required.
- IRDY# and DEVSEL# miss the PCI tVAL minimum (1.5 ns vs. 2 ns).
- The LPC controller may abort on delayed SYNC patterns.
- The SMB NEGACK bit misbehaves, and the SMBus hold time is too short.
- The GLPCI retry counter also counts other devices' retries.
- GPIO High Bank atomic writes clear non-selected bits after suspend.
- RTC CMOS RAM reads can return incorrect data.
- SSMIs may be asynchronous if an IRQ occurs at the same time.

**Debug and KEL**
- The GLIU debug port, pattern detection, and unexpected-address error flagging do not work.
- KEL CmdData, Snoop mode, and the AuxOutputFull bit behave incorrectly.

Many of these issues are described as having negligible or no operational impact.

Browns coach Kevin Stefanski said there is no single thing Shedeur Sanders must do to earn the backup quarterback job. He stressed his commitment to young players' development and doing what is right for them. Rookie Dillon Gabriel remains the starter, with Sanders and Bailey Zappe vying for the backup role. Stefanski's comments imply Sanders is still developing. Wide receiver Jerry Jeudy praised Sanders for being a pro and preparing for his opportunity. Sanders will likely remain the emergency third-string quarterback.

This study tested a learning-by-teaching approach to generative AI in physics. Students prompted, validated, and iteratively refined AI-produced simulations of physics phenomena. The authors hope the approach stays useful as AI evolves, and they extend earlier work showing that PhET simulations supported student learning.

**Methods**
- **Setting:** Spring 2025, a large R1 public university in the western United States, in the second semester of an algebra-based introductory physics for life sciences course (187 students initially enrolled).
- **Topic:** One laboratory session on electric potential and equipotential lines.
- **Groups:** Seven lab sections, taught by four teaching assistants, were assigned to three quasi-experimental conditions:
  - **Physical lab (control, N=27):** Equipment in a conductive solution.
  - **Prebuilt simulation (N=68):** A simulation designed by an author using AI tools.
  - **AI-engagement (N=66):** Students generated their own simulation with Claude (Sonnet 4, free version) from a provided initial prompt, then wrote their own follow-up prompts to validate and refine it.
- **Assessments:**
  - Five conceptual questions immediately after the lab.
  - Five Likert-scale attitude questions.
  - Midterm and final exam scores.
- **Analysis:** Residuals were not normally distributed, so nonparametric tests were used: Kruskal-Wallis, Dunn's, and Fisher's exact tests.

**Results**
- **Conceptual scores:** Scores differed significantly by condition (p<.001, η²=.359). Both simulation groups (median 80) outperformed the physical lab group (median 60), with no significant difference between the AI and prebuilt groups.
- **Exams:** Midterm and final scores did not differ significantly. The authors suggest that continued interactive instruction after the lab may explain why the post-lab differences did not persist.
- **Attitudes:** Both digital groups reported more positive attitudes than the physical lab group on all five questions. The AI and prebuilt groups differed only when comparing the lab to the previous week's lab, where the prebuilt group was more favorable. The authors attribute this possibly to the prebuilt simulation being faster and easier.
- **Student comments:** Students in both the AI and physical groups expressed frustration. Only the physical group indicated that the frustration hurt their learning.

**Discussion and limitations**
The authors conclude that AI-based simulation building can be added without cost to conceptual learning, despite the extra work and the risk of AI hallucination. They speculate that the validation process, encouraged by AI's imperfect outputs, may build scientific modeling skills.

Limitations include:
- Differences in the level of abstraction across conditions.
- Free-tier usage limits on the AI platform.
- Some students needing technical assistance.
- A single concept, a homogeneous student population, and one institution.

**Conclusions**
The authors present prebuilt simulations, AI-guided simulation development, and physical equipment as complementary approaches that should be matched to specific learning objectives. They call for careful implementation and further research on pedagogical framing.

This patent application describes an automated cryogenic storage system that stores and retrieves samples and transfers individual samples between cryogenic environments while keeping them below a cryogenic temperature threshold (e.g., −134°C, the glass transition of water).

**System components**
- **Storage vaults:** One or more vacuum-insulated vaults each hold many samples (e.g., 25,000) at about −150°C.
- **Sample handling module (SHM):** Connects the vaults to external ports where removable portable cryogenic workstations can dock.
- **Controller:** Manages transfers, refrigeration, humidity, calibration, sample identification and disaster recovery. It also maintains a database of sample locations.

**Sample transfer**
- The controller identifies a sample's origin and destination and determines the transfer type: workstation-to-vault, vault-to-workstation or vault-to-vault.
- A six-axis robot with a gripper moves samples quickly (e.g., under 5 or 15 seconds) through the SHM's non-cryogenic environment.
- The gripper uses picking fingers and an extendable insulating sleeve to protect samples in transit. It can also unlock and remove vault covers.
- Samples are verified by barcode scanning.

**Vault internals**
- Each vault contains a rack with two interleaved groups of rotating shelves, driven by motors mounted outside the vault.
- Pie-shaped trays hold up to 260 vials and are positioned by kinematic pins.
- A vertical shuttle driven by a leadscrew lifts trays to a threshold at the vault opening for robotic access.
- A temperature-adaptive PTFE bearing allows the rack to operate at both cryogenic and ambient temperatures.

**Refrigeration and humidity control**
- Primary and backup refrigeration coils circulate liquid nitrogen. Perforations in the coils release cold, dry gas that controls moisture.
- Exhaust gas is vented to the SHM and the docking port to control temperature and dew point.
- A cryo-drying system with a refrigerated cryotrap speeds humidity reduction after maintenance access.

**Other features**
- Portable workstations dock using datum and actuating pins and can hold samples at −150°C for up to 2 hours.
- A four-stage disaster recovery method addresses jammed trays, escalating from firmware reversal to full vault disassembly under an insulated shroud.
- The application also describes a camera module for ultra-low temperatures and an alternative star-shaped rack.

This cross-sectional study, posted as a medRxiv preprint that has not been peer reviewed, describes plasma Alzheimer disease (AD) biomarkers in elderly Amish individuals from Ohio and Indiana. These biomarkers had not previously been studied in this population. The Amish were chosen for their reduced genetic diversity and uniform environmental exposures.

**Methods**
- Data came from 1,067 participants (mean age 81.2) in the Collaborative Amish Aging and Memory Project.
- Participants were classified as cognitively unimpaired (CU), mild cognitive impairment (MCI), cognitively impaired but not AD (CINAD), or AD.
- Plasma Aβ40, Aβ42, total tau (t-tau), and p-tau181 were measured using Simoa assays, along with derived ratios.
- Associations were examined for two outcomes: AD and cognitive preservation (CP).
- Statistical methods included logistic regression, ROC analysis, and K-medoids clustering based on Aβ42/Aβ40 and p-tau181.

**Results**
- **Group differences:** Amyloid biomarkers did not differ between diagnostic groups. Individuals with AD had higher p-tau181 and a lower Aβ42/p-tau181 ratio than CU individuals.
- **AD association:** In multivariate analyses, no biomarker was significantly associated with AD overall. However, p-tau181 interacted with APOE ε4 and was strongly associated with AD only among ε4 carriers (OR = 6.02).
- **Cognitive preservation:** Higher Aβ42/Aβ40 was associated with CP (OR = 1.81, p = 0.05). When MCI was excluded, lower p-tau181 and a higher Aβ42/p-tau181 ratio were associated with CP.
- **Predictive models:** For distinguishing AD from CU, models using all biomarkers or Aβ42/p-tau181 performed best (AUC = 0.83). The best CP model combined APOE ε2 with all biomarkers (AUC up to 0.77). Models including t-tau performed poorest.
- **Clustering:** Two clusters emerged:
  - A low-risk group with higher Aβ42/Aβ40 and lower p-tau181.
  - A high-risk group with more APOE ε4 carriers and more individuals with AD.
  
  A three-cluster solution further separated individuals with low Aβ but high tau risk from those with moderate Aβ but low tau risk. The highest-risk cluster was linked to slower Trail Making B performance, but this did not survive multiple-testing correction.

**Limitations**
- The study population was small and not representative of the general population.
- No imaging or CSF data were available, so diagnoses may be misclassified.
- Plasma biomarkers serve only as proxies for brain pathology.
- The cross-sectional design limits conclusions about change over time.

**Conclusions**
The authors conclude that p-tau181, Aβ42/Aβ40, and Aβ42/p-tau181 are promising non-invasive indicators for distinguishing AD or cognitive impairment from CU in the Amish. Biomarker-guided clustering can identify individuals at varying AD risk. Longitudinal validation is needed.

STAT's Morning Rounds newsletter, headlined with the news that metal-organic frameworks won the chemistry Nobel (no details given), reports that Peter Marks, the FDA's former top vaccine regulator, has joined Eli Lilly to oversee molecule discovery and infectious diseases. Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. forced Marks to resign from the FDA in March. Marks said he is excited to help advance infectious disease products for public health. The rest of the newsletter is restricted to STAT+ subscribers.

A coach discusses his team's postseason play against San Jose.

**Team strengths**
- The team's puck-pursuit game wears opponents down by forcing defensemen to turn back for pucks.
- The team responds well to adversity, such as conceding goals, by continuing to play. The coach credits veteran players for leading this.
- His message is to play fast, make good puck decisions, avoid feeding the opponent's transition game, and stay patient, even if results take longer than three periods.
- Forward balance is a key strength, allowing any line to face any opponent. Bones' line, including penalty killer Haggy, is used against Pavelski's and Thornton's lines because it is defensively aware and an offensive threat.
- Defensively, the team blocked shot lanes and disrupted San Jose's strong low-zone possession, though this remains an area to keep working on.

**Players**
- **Sid** plays a complete, inspiring game. His unmatched work ethic and attention to detail explain his faceoff dominance.
- **Phil** shows little emotion and is an exceptional scorer. His line's chemistry and confidence have produced timely goals.
- **Geno** has had an emotional few days and is generating scoring chances. The coach expects him to score soon.
- **Conor**'s minutes are monitored to preserve his quickness, his competitive advantage, as he was wearing down. He has grown more comfortable with each call-up, helped by veteran mentorship.
- **Bryan** is a game-time decision.
- **Chris** has been effective through physical, proactive forechecking that creates turnovers.
- **Rusty** has the speed, tenacity, and compete level to score, and his confidence is high.
- An unnamed defenseman is valued for mobility, puck-moving, and offensive instincts.

**Coaching perspective**
The coach's player development role with the Hawks last year showed him how polished NHL players are. It taught him that patience helps young players develop.

The "Triangle Rotation" offense targets the triangle zone of the Triangle & Two defense, whose chasers excel at pass denial but whose zone rotations are usually weak. It uses simple clockwise and counterclockwise three-player rotations, bringing in the two shooters if inside rotations fail. Options include the point guard penetrating to an elbow while O4 pops out, a feed to O5 on a baseline cut, a weakside lob to O1, and side screens for the shooter. Success depends on execution, simplicity, zone-attack fundamentals and teamwork. Recommended strategies include scouting opponents, watching for defensive adjustments, varying alignments and attacking the weakest defenders.

In a message to Congress on the state of the Union, the President reports that the Nation has grown in strength, comfort, knowledge and education, and that peace is more assured. He describes current problems as problems of growth and progress.

**Foreign relations and defense:** Fifty-four nations have renounced war under the Kellogg-Briand pact. The World Court statute was amended to meet the Senate's reservations, and the President will submit the adherence protocol, stating it is no step toward League of Nations membership. A London naval limitation conference is planned.

Other foreign developments:
- **Mexico:** The arms embargo has been lifted.
- **Latin America:** The U.S. took part in the Tacna-Arica settlement and the Bolivia-Paraguay conciliation, and is mediating between Guatemala and Honduras. Regular air mail service to the region has begun.
- **Marines abroad:** About 1,600 remain in Nicaragua, 700 in Haiti (a commission is proposed) and 2,605 in China, with reductions hoped for.
- **Diplomacy:** Stronger Latin American missions and larger State Department appropriations are planned.

Defense spending has risen to over $730 million, exceeding that of the most militarized nations. Congress is urged to seek relief.

**Finances and taxes:** The public debt stands at $16.9 billion, down from a $26.6 billion peak. Recommended 1931 appropriations total $3.83 billion. Projected surpluses justify cutting individual normal income tax rates by one point and the corporate rate from 12 to 11 percent, saving taxpayers about $160 million.

Foreign debt settlements are nearly complete, with only Russia and Armenia unsettled. Funded debts total $11.58 billion, and an agreement with Germany on revised claims is forthcoming. Most seized alien property has been returned.

**Economy:** Speculation led to a stock market crash, reducing consumption and causing some temporary unemployment. The Federal reserve system and banks weathered the crisis. The President instituted voluntary cooperation to maintain wages, continue business and expand construction, and he believes confidence has been restored.

**Agriculture and tariff:** Farm income is rising, and the Federal Farm Board is organizing cooperative marketing. The President supports limited tariff revision, agricultural protection and a more efficient flexible tariff, stressing national unity.

**Infrastructure and transport:**
- **Public buildings:** Expanded authorizations are recommended, along with Fine Arts Commission review of adjacent private buildings.
- **Waterways:** Larger rivers, harbors and Mississippi flood control appropriations are proposed, while the Atchafalaya floodway is withheld for review.
- **Highways:** Increased federal aid for farm-to-market roads is suggested.
- **Post Office:** Its deficit exceeds $80 million, prompting study of leases and air mail rates.
- **Aviation:** Commercial aviation has grown remarkably.
- **Railroads:** They are in good condition, but consolidation legislation and relief for the Commission from minor matters are needed.
- **Merchant marine:** Larger mail contracts requiring new vessels are proposed.

**Regulation and resources:**
- **Banking:** A joint commission should study group and chain banking and branch banking.
- **Federal Power Commission:** Full-time commissioners and limited interstate authority are recommended.
- **Radio Commission:** It should become permanent without zone-based appointments.
- **Muscle Shoals:** A commission should negotiate leases, dedicating benefits to agricultural chemistry research.
- **Boulder Dam:** Funds should be appropriated once contracts are ready.
- **Public lands:** Abuses in oil permits, overgrazing and reclamation policy are referred to a new conservation commission.

**Social policy:**
- **Social services:** Federal activity should stay limited to preserve local responsibility. Conferences on child health, housing and education are planned.
- **Public health:** Federal support for local health units through the states is recommended.
- **Prisons:** New prisons, a Bureau of Prisons and parole reform are needed.
- **Immigration:** Quotas should consider immigrant fitness.
- **Veterans:** Veterans' agencies should be consolidated.
- **Civil service:** It should cover third-class postmasters.
- **Reorganization:** Congress should delegate departmental reorganization authority to the Executive.

**Law enforcement:** Prohibition enforcement should be strengthened by moving detection to the Justice Department, simplifying petty prosecutions, codifying the laws and unifying border patrol under the Coast Guard. The District of Columbia also needs remedies. A national commission is studying law enforcement, and the President calls for citizen respect for law.

The message concludes that decisions should be judged by whether they advance American ideals.

Alex Ovechkin says receiving the award means a lot to him and calls it "history." He thanks his teammates, coaching staff and family, describing the year as difficult because he switched to right wing midseason. He credits Adam, whom he says he trusted from the first day, with the move, saying he would never have played right wing without him. He had played left wing in the KHL and could have returned to it if things went badly, but the switch worked, including on the power play. He still wants to compete for the Stanley Cup, noting he won this award but lost the Cup.

Ovechkin says his foot is fine, and he plans to start playing tennis soon. He explains that a blocked shot broke his foot, which an MRI confirmed after he returned from the Russian national team. He played through it with injections because playoff hockey demands it, noting that players from L.A. and Detroit are now having surgery after playing injured. He praises Washington's trainers for understanding his body. He says he would never refuse to play if he could skate and hold his stick.

Michael Johnson, 61, provost and marketing professor at Babson College, has been named John Carroll University's president, its first lay leader since its founding by the Society of Jesuits 131 years ago. The board approved a five-year contract on Dec. 6, and salary details were not released. He begins July 1, replacing the retiring Rev. Robert Niehoff, and will also join the faculty. Johnson previously taught at Michigan for 24 years and was a dean at Cornell for 10 years.

Two $25 million government studies, conducted by the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences at the FDA's request, exposed rats and mice to very high doses of cellphone radiation nine hours daily for up to two years. They found a small increase in a rare heart nerve-tissue tumor in male rats but no significant problems in female rats or mice. There was no hard evidence of brain tumors, which preliminary results had hinted at, and only "equivocal evidence" of DNA damage and some cancers. Exposed rats unexpectedly lived longer. Lead author John Bucher said the doses far exceeded typical use and the findings do not translate directly to humans. The FDA and the American Cancer Society's Otis Brawley said cellphones remain safe, though Brawley suggested earpieces for concerned users. UCLA's Leeka Kheifets noted some concerning activity but no large effect. Critic David Carpenter said the studies were too small and that excessive use poses some hazard. Most prior human studies found little evidence of risk.

A King's College London analysis of 49 studies involving 266,939 people found that regular physical activity was linked to lower odds of developing depression in children, adults and older adults, even after accounting for factors like BMI and smoking. Researchers plan to study activity types and "dosages" and call for policy change.

This institution-based cross-sectional study assessed awareness of, and attitudes toward, labor epidural analgesia (LEA) among third-trimester pregnant women planning vaginal delivery at Hemen Medical Center, a private facility in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. It also examined factors influencing their decision to use LEA. The authors note that LEA is considered the gold standard for labor pain relief but remains underused in developing regions, including Ethiopia, where no prior published studies on this topic exist.

**Methods**
- Data were collected from June 3 to August 30, 2024, using self-administered questionnaires.
- Of 267 women sampled systematically, 230 were analyzed.
- Analysis used descriptive statistics and logistic regression.

**Participants**
- Mean age was 29.9 years.
- 66.6% held a degree or higher.
- About half were nulliparous.

**Awareness and attitudes**
- 78% had heard of LEA, mainly from previous users, family and friends, and the internet.
- Only 6.5% cited healthcare providers as their primary source.
- Only 34% received explanations about LEA during antenatal care.
- 47% believed LEA was effective, yet only 14.3% were willing to use it.
- Main concerns were maternal side effects, fetal safety, interference with natural labor, and cost.

**Factors associated with choosing LEA**
In multivariable analysis, the following were significantly associated with the decision:
- Higher education
- Monthly family income above 25,000 ETB
- Perceived fetal risk (associated with refusal)
- Belief in LEA's pain-relief effectiveness

**Limitations**
- Single-center setting
- Inability to assess prior epidural experience
- Cross-sectional design, which prevented tracking actual LEA use

**Conclusion**
The authors conclude that hesitancy despite high awareness may reflect inadequate explanations from healthcare providers. They recommend comprehensive education and counseling during antenatal care.

This patent application, a continuation of earlier U.S. applications claiming priority to a March 25, 2016 provisional filing, covers specific deuterated heterocycle fused gamma-carbolines. It includes their free, salt (e.g., tosylate) and substantially pure forms, pharmaceutical compositions, and methods of treating diseases involving 5-HT2A receptors, the serotonin transporter (SERT) and/or dopamine D receptor pathways.

**Background**
- Schizophrenia and related psychoses affect an estimated 1–2% of the global population.
- Residual-phase symptoms (negative symptoms, cognitive dysfunction, depression, insomnia) are poorly treated by many current antipsychotics.
- There is also a need for drugs free of side effects from histamine H1 and muscarinic receptor interactions.
- Prior patents disclose related gamma-carbolines, their salts, prodrugs and generic deuterated versions.

**Discovery and compounds**
- The applicants found that the major metabolic routes of the compound of Formula Q are N-dealkylation, alpha-oxidation at the piperazine ring and carbonyl reduction.
- The resulting alcohol metabolite retains significant activity.
- The invention provides compounds (Formulas I–IV) with a trideuterated N-methyl and/or a di-deuterated methylene adjacent to the N-methyl.
- These compounds antagonize 5-HT2A receptors, inhibit serotonin reuptake and modulate dopaminergic protein phosphorylation like their non-deuterated analogs, but with unexpectedly improved metabolic stability.
- Embodiments specify diastereomeric purity and deuterium incorporation levels.

**Compositions**
- Immediate, sustained or delayed release formulations.
- Injectable depot formulations in polymeric matrices (preferably PLGA) releasing drug over up to 180 days.
- Osmotic-controlled release oral delivery systems.

**Methods of treatment**
- Target conditions include:
  - dementia-related disorders and agitation
  - schizophrenia and residual psychosis symptoms
  - depression and anxiety
  - sleep disorders
  - PTSD and impulse control disorders
  - dyskinesia
  - autism
- Typical oral doses are about 1–100 mg daily, or 1–10 mg for sleep and related disorders.
- Combinations are described with antipsychotics, antidepressants, GABA modulators, cholinesterase inhibitors, memantine and other agents, potentially at reduced doses.

**Examples**
- Syntheses of three deuterated compounds and a comparative internal standard are described.
- **Mice:** Relative amide metabolite formation was 0.54, 0.38 and 0.31 for Examples 1–3, versus 0.79 for non-deuterated compound Q. Receptor binding was substantially the same as Q's.
- **Rats (oral dosing):** For Q, metabolite Q-1 exposure was 2.2-fold that of the parent. For Example 2, it was 1.2-fold, a 55% decrease in relative metabolism.
- **Dogs (sublingual dosing):** Example 2 gave about 72% higher parent exposure than Q, and amide metabolite Q-1 was undetectable. Subcutaneous dosing produced comparable parent exposure for both compounds.

This systematic review assessed the accuracy and validity of ChatGPT's responses in education. ChatGPT, developed by OpenAI, evolved from GPT-1 (2018) to GPT-4 (March 2023) and gained over a million users within a week of launch. Prior research identifies potential benefits, including personalised learning, feedback, assessment creation and skill development. It also identifies concerns about plagiarism, cheating, bias, inaccuracy, undetectable machine writing and effects on higher-order thinking.

**Method:** Following PRISMA guidelines, the author searched Google Scholar, Web of Science and EBSCO using "ChatGPT + Education." Only peer-reviewed, empirical, English-language studies were included. Eighteen studies were reviewed using thematic analysis. They covered fields such as medicine, writing assignments, business, finance, chemistry, academic advising, physics, social science and programming.

**Results:** Two categories emerged.
* **Writing:** ChatGPT produced coherent, well-structured, precise and sometimes creative text, at times exceeding the quality of high school and university students' work. However, responses sometimes lacked depth, argumentation and case-specific detail. Teachers and students had difficulty identifying ChatGPT-written essays.
* **Performance as a learner:** ChatGPT passed many undergraduate and medical exams, but it performed poorly on advanced finance problems, complex chemistry problems and some medical tests. It gave false information confidently, hallucinated, produced repetitive or inconsistent answers and struggled with calculations, nuance and non-textual prompts.

**Discussion:** ChatGPT performs like a beginner undergraduate and excels at essay-based tasks. Its effectiveness in science is limited because it is designed to generate human-like text and was trained on internet data up to 2021.

**Implications:** The author recommends the following:
* validating ChatGPT's responses
* using carefully structured text prompts
* redesigning assessments to target higher-order skills
* developing institutional policies
* training students in constructive use

The author also proposes an "ABCD framework" for adopting ChatGPT in education.

**Conclusion and limitations:** ChatGPT shows educational potential but lacks deep understanding and accuracy in complex scientific and calculation tasks. The author suggests cooperation between educational institutions and developers on an education-specific ChatGPT, and further research on customised GPTs. The review was limited to specific databases, accessible studies and searches up to 26 October 2023.

The "Four Down" (also "Four Low" or "Four Flat") is a spread offense used mainly for last shots in a period, but effective for any team with a talented ballhandler. The ballhandler calls it by pointing four fingers downward. The four other players line the baseline, best shooters in the corners, isolating the ballhandler one-on-one. The ballhandler drives or pulls up, passing to open posts if baseline defenders help or to corner shooters if wing defenders sag. Under pressure, corners pop out for release passes and may take over the ballhandler role. Crunch-time options include the Mid Screen (a post screens for the ballhandler, creating drive, jumper, roll or kick-out options), the Triple Base Screen (staggered baseline screens for a shooter, best with four seconds left) and the Misdirection Double (a weakside double screen paired with a dribble handoff).

The 2-3 zone is the most commonly used zone defense. Its alignment keeps big players inside, making it strong at protecting the basket, stopping dribble penetration, and defending poor outside shooting teams, but vulnerable to good outside shooters. It is often chosen by teams at a disadvantage in quickness, athleticism, and skill, yet quick players can make it an aggressive trapping defense. It also works well against talented or big low post players.

**Alignment and roles**
- **Guards:** Two guards play side by side above the free throw line. They move in unison from sideline to sideline, so they are usually the team's quickest players.
- **Post:** The post stays in front of the basket, between the ball and the basket. This role usually goes to the biggest player.
- **Baseline players:** Two baseline players start outside the three-second area above the blocks. They work opposite each other, with one always in a weakside rebounding position, so they should be skilled rebounders.
- **All defenders:** Everyone keeps arms extended and shifts while passes are in the air.

**Shifts and adjustments**
- The passage details shifts for the ball in the middle, on each wing, and in each corner.
- On corner passes, the wing defender may either deny the return pass or drop to help on the post, at the coach's discretion.
- Reversal or skip passes are the zone's difficult shift. A baseline defender temporarily "shows" on the ball until a guard arrives.

**1-1-3 variation**
- The guard opposite the best shooter takes the ballhandler.
- In a tandem alignment, the point defender extends pressure, forces early wing entries, and pushes the ball away from the best shooter.

**Trap options**
- Corner traps, surprise point traps, and automatic wing traps against a star shooter.

**Defending a dominant post ("Footer")**
- The post defender uses pass denial, teammates provide backside and topside support, and the defense double- or triple-teams the post upon entry.

This excerpt from the UC1825B-SP datasheet (Texas Instruments, revised December 2020) covers design, layout, and documentation information.

**Sense resistor:** It senses transformer ripple current and shuts down the switching cycle if peak current exceeds the set limit. The CS pin threshold is about 1 V, and the shutdown current should exceed the maximum expected current, which depends on the design.

**Test results:** Figures show MOSFET voltage stress, output ripple, and a 0-A to 10-A load transient, all tested at 48-V input and 10-A output.

**Power supply and topologies:** The device operates from a well-regulated 10-V to 30-V supply. If the supply is more than a few inches away, additional bulk capacitance, typically a 100-μF tantalum capacitor, may be needed. Supported topologies include push-pull, forward, half-bridge, and full bridge.

**Layout guidelines:**
- **Inductors:** Use low-EMI, closed-core ferrite inductors and avoid stick cores.
- **Feedback traces:** Route them directly, away from inductors and noisy traces, ideally on the opposite PCB side with a ground plane between.
- **Capacitors and compensation components:** Place input, feed-forward, and compensation parts close to the IC, preferably surface-mount and away from the inductor.
- **Power traces:** Keep them short and thick, with at least 15 mils per ampere, and use one via per 200 mA.
- **Switching loops:** Arrange them to conduct in the same direction to reduce EMI.
- **Grounding:** Use a ground plane with a dedicated power ground for 2-A peak driver currents. Bypass VCC to power ground and VREF and analog circuitry to signal ground.

**Additional content:** The excerpt also covers documentation update notifications, E2E support forums, ESD handling cautions, packaging notes (a hermetically sealed metal-lid package), and TI's legal disclaimers.

In Community Board 7 of the Borough of Manhattan v Schaffer (argued April 26, 1994; decided June 16, 1994), the New York Court of Appeals considered whether a community board created by the New York City Charter had the capacity to bring an article 78 proceeding challenging the denial of its Freedom of Information Law (FOIL) request.

**Background.** In 1990, the board, which represents a Manhattan district that includes the Penn Central railyards, requested documents from the Department of City Planning about the proposed "Trump City" project, including its draft "restrictive declaration" and related correspondence. The Department denied the request, citing FOIL exemptions for inter- and intra-agency materials and potential impairment of contract awards. The Supreme Court ruled the board had standing and ordered disclosure, and the Appellate Division affirmed.

**Mootness.** The Court declined to dismiss for mootness, even though the project had been scaled down, the board's review was complete, and the request was withdrawn. It found the issue likely to recur, likely to evade review, and novel and substantial.

**Decision.** Writing for a unanimous Court, Judge Titone distinguished capacity (a litigant's power to sue) from standing (a sufficient stake in the outcome). Legislatively created entities may sue only with express statutory authority or by necessary implication, absent contrary legislative intent. Although the board had "functional responsibility" within the zone of interest protected by the Uniform Land Use Review Procedure (ULURP), the Court found it lacked capacity for several reasons:

- The Charter gives community boards no power to sue, retain independent counsel, or subpoena documents.
- ULURP specifies which documents boards receive.
- During the 1975 Charter revision, recommendations to grant boards the power to sue were not adopted, and the relevant provision was reenacted without substantive change.
- The boards' advisory role does not require such power.

FOIL's broad standing provisions did not cure the lack of capacity. The judgment was reversed and the petition dismissed.

The passage, from a Texas Instruments ADS9803 data sheet, covers device operation, register configuration, application guidance, and support information.

**Power-down and initialization:** The device powers down through a logic 0 on the PWDN pin or by writing 11b to the PD_CH field. After power-up or reset, it is initialized with a sequence of register writes while a free-running sampling clock is connected. Users can then change the analog input range, bandwidth, common-mode voltage range, and the number of data output lanes.

**Speed-boost mode:** This mode allows up to 8MSPS for one user-selected channel pair. That pair is converted on every sampling clock, and the other six channels stay idle.

**SPI register access:** The 16-bit registers are grouped into three banks with 8-bit addresses.
- Bank 0 is always accessible. Banks 1 and 2 are selected through REG_BANK_SEL at address 0x03.
- Writes require SPI_RD_EN = 0b.
- Reads require SPI_RD_EN = 1b and SPI_MODE = 1b and follow a defined multi-frame sequence.

**Daisy-chain topology:** Multiple ADCs share the CS and SCLK lines, with each SDO connected to the next device's SDI.
- DAISY_CHAIN_LEN equals the number of ADCs excluding the first.
- Each write requires N × 24 SCLKs, and reads follow a specified two-step frame procedure.

**Register map:** The descriptions cover data format, averaging, XOR/PRBS operation, digital test patterns, speed-boost settings, 21-bit gain error correction codes, analog input bandwidth, power-down, reference selection, output lane mode, and common-mode range control.

**Application example (ATE):** The ADS9803 is described as an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS data acquisition system with a built-in analog front-end.
- It achieves 0.0015% total unadjusted error at 25°C ±5°C after calibration.
- Its wide-bandwidth mode settles to 99.95% of full scale in 7.5µs, which supports multiplexed PMU signals.

**Power and layout:** The device uses three supplies (AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, and IOVDD) with no required power-up sequence. Layout guidance calls for 0.1μF bypass capacitors placed close to the supply pins and separation of analog and digital signals.

**Remaining content:** The passage also includes documentation update notifications, E2E support forums, ESD cautions, packaging notes, and TI legal disclaimers.

Europe's ageing population poses rising health and social care costs, and the tax-paying population may be unable to fund care programs from 2030 onwards. The authors argue that current strategic plans are poorly grounded in facts and often stall at the pilot stage. They propose a three-step approach:

1. **Proactive prevention** aimed at the "young elderly" (aged 60–75), who make up 18–23% of the population in most EU countries (about 97 million people by 2020), to keep them healthy, active and independent past 75.
2. **Intervention tools** in the form of smartphone-based digital wellness services.
3. **Commercial ecosystems** to sustain these services, since research projects alone are not enough.

Wellness was chosen over health because wellness services avoid strictly regulated health data. The authors use four wellness dimensions (intellectual, physical, social and emotional), which mirror the dimensions of functional impairment and may compensate for one another.

The Finnish BeWell research program (2014–16) develops these services through action design research, co-creating them with users rather than for them. The technology combines:
- **Wellmo**, an "omnivore" platform originally developed by Nokia that connects to 100+ devices and applications.
- **Tieto's cloud platform**, which provides scalable advanced analytics and data fusion and can support coach-like advice.

About 100 workshops showed that the young elderly are experienced and not easily impressed by technology, but they have time for activities they find worthwhile. A survey in the Åland Islands (101 respondents) found that:
- About 73% use smartphones.
- Mobile app users are confident with apps, and the respondents rate wellness, especially intellectual challenges, as important.
- Education, age, work status, income and gender produced significant differences in attitudes.

The authors conclude that the young elderly are a viable, overlooked user group for mobile services. They also find that digital business provides the environment for sustainable services and that services should be designed with users on omnivore platforms. Because the sample is small and regional, the findings require validation with a larger sample.

This excerpt from the Texas Instruments ADS8681W/ADS8685W/ADS8689W data sheet covers reference options, transfer function, alarms, digital interface, registers, application design, power, and layout.

**External Reference:** Setting the INTREF_DIS bit to 1 selects external reference mode. A 4.096V reference is applied at REFIO, and an internal buffer drives REFCAP. REFCAP requires a minimum 10µF capacitor plus a 1µF decoupling capacitor. The buffer must not drive external loads. Its drift is typically 0.5ppm/°C (maximum 2ppm/°C) across –40°C to +125°C.

**Transfer Function:** The device supports single-ended and differential inputs with bipolar and unipolar ranges. Output is in straight-binary format, and LSB = FSR / 2^16.

**Alarms:** The ALARM/SDO-1/GPO pin provides an active-high alarm when SDO1_CONFIG is set to 01b.
- **Input alarm:** Compares the input against programmable high and low thresholds, with common hysteresis.
- **AVDD alarm:** Uses fixed thresholds of 4.7V and 5.3V.
- **Flags:** Each alarm has an active flag, cleared after each conversion, and a tripped flag, cleared when ALARM_REG is read.
- **Reading flags:** Flags can be read via the pin, the registers, or appended to the output data.

**Digital Interface:** The multiSPI interface appears to the host as a 32-bit shift register.
- **Topologies:** Supported configurations include all multiSPI options, standard SPI, and daisy-chain. Daisy-chain requires identical register values and 32 × N SCLK edges, and it reduces throughput.

**Operating States:**
- **RESET:** The RST pin issues either a power-on reset (default) or an application reset, selected by the RSTn_APP bit.
- **ACQ:** The device acquires the input signal.
- **CONV:** Conversion is triggered by the CONVST/CS rising edge and uses an internal clock.

**Programming:**
- **Frames:** Data frames begin on the CONVST/CS falling edge. Frames of 32 or more SCLKs yield valid commands, while shorter frames are treated as NOP but still output valid MSBs.
- **Commands:** Supported commands include byte and half-word read, write, set, and clear operations.
- **Output word:** Contains conversion data, register data, or fixed patterns. Optional appended flags include device address, range, alarms, and parity.

**Data Transfer Protocols:**
- **Write:** Uses four SPI modes (SPI-00-S to SPI-11-S), with SPI-00-S as the default.
- **Read:** Supports SPI with single or dual SDO, or source-synchronous protocols with internal or external clock options.

**Registers:** The device has nine configuration registers controlling device ID, reset and power, SDI and SDO protocols, data output, range and reference, alarm flags, and alarm thresholds. Writes to RST_PWRCTL_REG require first writing 69h to address 05h.

**Application Example:** An eight-channel PLC input module pairs the ADS8681W with the MUX36D08 multiplexer for industrial ranges up to ±10V and 4–20mA. The device settles to 1% in under 5µs. Input alarm hysteresis with an NTC thermistor prevents false temperature alarms.

**Power:**
- **Supplies:** Separate AVDD and DVDD supplies require decoupling, which improves PSRR.
- **NAP mode:** Reduces power in the ACQ state.
- **Power-down mode:** Powers down analog blocks while retaining register contents.

**Layout:** Recommendations include separating analog and digital sections, placing bypass capacitors close to the pins without vias, and using specified REFCAP and REFIO capacitors.

The document also includes support, ESD caution, revision history, and legal information.

This medRxiv preprint (not peer reviewed) describes the introduction, spread and evolution of SARS-CoV-2 Alpha and Delta variants in Vietnam in 2021, and how they related to public health measures.

**Background:** Vietnam largely controlled SARS-CoV-2 in 2020, with 1,465 confirmed cases and 35 deaths. It relied on border restrictions, contact tracing, mass testing, quarantine and public communication. Importations of the Alpha and then Delta variants in early 2021 led to over 1.7 million infections and 32,000 deaths by year's end.

**Methods:** Nasopharyngeal swabs from locally acquired cases were sequenced at two tertiary hospitals in Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City. The researchers then performed lineage classification, phylogenetic analysis, Bayesian phylogeographic and phylodynamic analysis of the Delta AY.57 lineage, and selection pressure (dN/dS) estimation.

**Results:**
- **Sequencing:** Of 1,365 samples, 1,303 genomes were obtained, with no recombinants. Delta accounted for 93.8%, Alpha for 5.7%, and A.23.1 and B.1.637 for the remainder. AY.57 made up 99.2% of Delta sequences.
- **Alpha:** Sequences formed four clusters, indicating multiple introductions between January and May 2021. Community transmission was not sustained, likely due to rigorous containment.
- **Delta emergence:** Delta was first detected in late April 2021 and was the only variant found from June onward, coinciding with the outbreak surge.
- **Delta spread:** AY.57 was introduced into the Northeast region, with an estimated common ancestor dated March 14, 2021. It spread to other regions, especially the southeast, which later reseeded the north and the rest of the country.
- **Localized clusters:** Viral dispersal between provinces was infrequent, and distinct localized clusters formed. This was possibly influenced by strict lockdowns and travel restrictions.
- **Genetic diversity:** Diversity rose sharply between April and August 2021 in a largely unvaccinated, immunologically naïve population, then remained relatively stable.
- **Selection and evolution:** Overall dN/dS was 0.86, indicating weak purifying selection, with positive selection in ORF1b, ORF3a, E and ORF7a. The evolutionary rate was 5.29×10⁻⁴ substitutions per site per year.

**Limitations:** Referral-hospital sampling may have missed co-circulating variants, though the authors consider this unlikely.

**Conclusion:** Public health measures contained Alpha, but Delta AY.57 caused an explosive outbreak. The authors conclude that genomic surveillance is critical to inform pandemic response.

This preprint uses a mathematical thought experiment to test whether a screening-isolation strategy can control an untreatable infectious disease in a semi-isolated community during a global pandemic, when vaccines and medications are unavailable.

The authors adapted the SIR model so that new infections come from local transmission and outside influx, and losses come from screening-isolation efficiency (η), recovery/death (γ = 0.3) and a time lag (ν) between infection and isolation. Theoretical analysis showed that control requires a short time lag. A large lag lets the epidemic escape control, and improving screening efficiency contributes only weakly to robustness.

Poisson-based simulations produced these results:

- **Daily screening (η = 0.9, influx m = 0.1):**
  - With R0 = 3.0, infection was controlled. Waves had no more than 10 infections and lasted an average of 1.64 days. Without screening, the disease spread out of control within 100 days.
  - Control still held at R0 = 6.0 but failed at R0 = 8.0. The authors suggest combining screening with measures such as social distancing and mask use.
- **Screening frequency (R0 = 3.0):**
  - Every 3 days kept infections controlled, at about 267 cases per year (η = 0.7) and 143 cases per year (η = 0.9).
  - Weekly screening performed much worse, with about 36,100 cases per year at η = 0.7 and 575 at η = 0.9.
  - Screening every two weeks failed at both efficiencies.
- **Border control:** Annual infections rose in proportion to influx, at about 15, 157 and 2,025 cases for m = 0.01, 0.1 and 1. This indicates strict border control is necessary.

The discussion notes that fever screening has variable effectiveness, while PCR-based tests are highly sensitive and suitable for community-wide screening. Detectability before transmission begins improves control. Remaining challenges include disruption to community operations and residents' psychological problems.

The authors conclude that periodic screening can control transmission, with infection size affected by screening frequency, screening efficiency and migration rate.

This systematic review, a non-peer-reviewed medRxiv preprint, examined how marijuana (MJ) and cannabinoids affect the human microbiome. Background evidence cited includes cannabinoids' anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive properties, the gut microbiota's role in inflammation and the gut-brain axis, and preclinical findings that cannabis alters gut bacteria.

**Methods**
- The review was registered on PROSPERO (CRD42022354331) and followed PRISMA guidelines.
- PubMed, Embase and Cochrane were searched up to July 20, 2022.
- Animal, in vitro and non-peer-reviewed studies were excluded.
- Risk of bias was assessed with the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and ROBINS-I.

**Studies included**
- Of 4,022 articles identified, 9 studies were included: 1 case-control, 6 cohort and 2 clinical trials.
- They covered 2,526 participants aged 17–101, from the USA, Iran, Israel and the UK, spanning 1983–2021.
- Most participants were women, and cognitive impairment was the most common patient condition.

**Key findings**
- **HIV:** MJ use was associated with increased Fusobacterium and Anaerotruncus and decreased Dorea. Among women, gonorrhea was more prevalent in those with recurrent bacterial vaginosis (5% vs 1.3%).
- **Inflammation:** During exercise, increases in the endocannabinoids AEA and PEA correlated with reduced TNF-α and IL-6. They mediated about one-third of the effect of short-chain fatty acids on these cytokines.
- **Obesity:** The endocannabinoid OEA significantly reduced energy and nutrient intake and increased A. muciniphila.
- **Cognition:** Mitochondrial function correlated with cognitive scores in MJ users. Greater lifetime use tended toward a lower Prevotella:Bacteroides ratio, alongside dietary changes.
- **Oral microbiome:** Daily or near-daily MJ inhalation correlated with oral microbiome differences. Causation was not established, and the changes were not consistent with malignancy.
- **Musculoskeletal pain:** S. mutans and Lactobacilli rose by week 4 of medical cannabis treatment.
- **Adverse events:** 21.4% of patients in one study reported coughing or wheezing from MJ cigarettes, and one patient developed systemic aspergillosis. All effects resolved after stopping smoking.

**Conclusion**
A meta-analysis was not possible because the studies covered varied pathological conditions. Literature on these interactions is limited, and further research is warranted. The study was funded by Thailand's Department of Thai Traditional and Alternative Medicine.

In this State of the Union address, the speaker reports that America is much improved and calls for bipartisan cooperation to continue its renewal.

**Progress cited**
- The 1970s brought rising inflation, high taxes, expanding regulation and lost international respect.
- Since then, inflation has fallen from 12.4 to 3.2 percent, and the prime rate has been nearly halved.
- An across-the-board tax cut was passed, and tax indexing begins next year.
- Four million Americans found jobs in 1983.
- Military pride has been restored.
- The speaker acknowledges that many people remain unemployed.

**Four goals for the 1980s**

1. **Economic growth**
   - Reduce deficits by limiting government rather than raising taxes, which the speaker calls a "Band-Aid solution."
   - Defense spending, less than a third of the budget, should not bear further cuts.
   - Seek a bipartisan "down payment" of about $100 billion in deficit reduction over three years through spending cuts, closing tax loopholes and Grace Commission savings.
   - Pursue structural spending reforms, a line-item veto and a balanced-budget amendment.
   - Have Secretary Don Regan prepare a tax-simplification plan by December 1984.

2. **Developing the next frontier**
   - Direct NASA to build a permanently manned space station within a decade, inviting other countries to participate.
   - Promote private launch services.
   - Increase EPA funding, including cleanup of the Chesapeake Bay and hazardous waste sites, extension of Superfund, doubled acid rain research and $157 million for park and conservation lands.

3. **Strengthening traditional values**
   - Improve education through parental and local responsibility, discipline, merit rewards, tougher standards and tuition tax credits.
   - Restore school prayer and legal protection for unborn children.
   - Fight crime, child pornography and abuse.
   - Support fair housing, women's rights and enterprise zones.

4. **Lasting peace**
   - Pursue stable relations with the Soviet Union, nuclear arms reductions and stronger alliances.
   - Continue peacemaking in the Middle East, Central America and southern Africa, including the peacekeeping mission in Lebanon.
   - Propose anti-terrorism legislation and seek freer world trade.
   - The speaker tells the Soviet people that "a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought."

**Closing**
The speaker honors Sergeant Stephen Trujillo for his heroism in Grenada, as well as Father Ritter and Dr. Charles Carson. He concludes that America's best days lie ahead.

This study reports theoretical evidence for an intervalley superconducting phase in the half-filled second moiré bands (hole filling νh = 3) of approximately 2°-twisted bilayer MoTe2. The authors performed exact diagonalization on a continuum model that includes both valleys, Coulomb intravalley interactions, and intervalley interactions screened over an effective length d. Hartree–Fock calculations accounted for corrections from the emptied first moiré bands.

**Phase diagram as d increases**
- **Ferromagnetic Chern insulator:** stable for d < dc,1 ≈ 0.15 aM.
- **Intermediate phase:** appears between dc,1 and dc,2, with a singly degenerate paramagnetic ground state and 2π-periodic spectral flow.
- **Non-Abelian fractional spin Hall insulator:** stable for d > dc,2 ≈ 0.33 aM, showing ground-state degeneracy and 4π-periodic spectral flow.

**Evidence that the intermediate phase is a superconductor**
- The ground state has zero total magnetization and momentum.
- Intervalley entanglement entropy is large.
- Binding energy is negative, with its magnitude maximized in this region.
- The pair density matrix shows a single dominant eigenvalue.
- Superfluid stiffness is finite.
- The order parameter indicates time-reversal-symmetric, nodal extended s-wave pairing.
- Intervalley exciton condensation was ruled out.

**Transition and field theory**
The transition at dc,2 appears continuous, with topology and symmetry changing simultaneously. The authors describe it with a Chern-Simons field theory in which condensing a matter field reduces the Pf × Pf topological order to a superconductor.

**Role of quantum geometry**
Replacing the moiré bands with idealized first Landau levels makes superconductivity much less apparent. Introducing non-uniform quantum geometry restores it, highlighting the importance of band geometry.

**Experimental outlook**
The authors suggest that tuning d through gating or substrate engineering could make the superconducting phase experimentally accessible.

Over-the-counter (OTC) trading is conducted directly between two parties without a centralized exchange. It takes place electronically through decentralized networks of market makers and dealers. Stocks, bonds, derivatives, commodities, ETFs and currencies all trade OTC, with more than 12,000 securities traded on the US OTC market.

**Who uses it**
- OTC stocks typically belong to small companies that cannot meet exchange listing requirements or that choose to avoid listing fees and reporting rules.
- Some large foreign companies, such as Nestle, trade OTC via American Depository Receipts.
- In the US, the main networks are managed by OTC Markets Group and regulated by FINRA, though less stringently than major exchanges.

**Benefits**
- Contracts can be customized, which suits hedging with derivatives.
- Small companies gain access to capital.
- Overall market liquidity increases.

**Risks**
- Transparency, liquidity and reporting requirements are lower than on exchanges.
- Counterparty risk is significant.
- The market is susceptible to manipulation, fraud and pump-and-dump schemes.
- The OTC-traded mortgage-backed securities and derivatives that caused the 2007/2008 crisis led FINRA to introduce clearinghouses.

**Crypto**
Crypto mostly trades on exchanges, but OTC desks handle large off-market deals, and peer-to-peer platforms also exist.

**Returns**
- Penny stocks average a negative 24% annual return, over 90% fail, and fewer than 1% move to major exchanges.
- A study of 10,000 OTC stocks from 2001 to 2010 found an average loss of 27% and a median loss of 37%.
- Thin trading causes high slippage.

The authors conclude that investing in, short-term trading or day trading OTC stocks is inadvisable.

This patent disclosure, a continuation of earlier U.S. applications, describes a method for transmitting and receiving sounding reference signals (SRS) in wireless communication systems, focusing on configuring and indicating guard periods for SRS antenna switching.

**Problem:** UEs that perform SRS antenna switching (e.g., 1T4R, 1T2R, 2T4R) need transition time when the transmission antenna for another uplink channel (PUSCH or PUCCH) differs from the SRS transmission antenna. Without a guard period, adjacent transmissions may suffer performance deterioration.

**Core method:** The UE receives SRS configuration information from a base station, including SRS resources and their usage. A guard period of Y symbols is configured for the SRS resources. Its length depends on subcarrier spacing and may be one or two symbols. When the guard period overlaps a specific uplink channel, such as a PUCCH for CSI reporting or beam failure recovery, the priority between the guard period and that channel matches the priority between the SRS and that channel. If the PUCCH is for beam failure recovery, the overlapping guard period and SRS resource may be dropped.

**First embodiment (guard period relative to PUSCH/PUCCH):**
- The guard period may be configured via RRC, MAC-CE, or DCI.
- Configuration may specify the start position, number of symbols, and whether a gap exists before or after the SRS.
- When no guard period is configured, the UE uses the same transmission beam for adjacent transmissions, indicated by SRI and/or TPMI.
- Options for resolving collisions include grouping SRS resources with Y symbols under shared priority rules, dropping the SRS group or the PUCCH, puncturing, rate matching, or shifting SRS symbols.
- The UE may also determine the guard period itself and report it to the base station.

**Second embodiment (collisions between guard periods and SRS resource sets):**
- Y symbols may be configured per SRS resource set.
- Collisions may be resolved by priority rules based on DCI timing, periodicity, or set usage.
- Other options include partial or full dropping of SRS groups, restructuring SRS groups, or deferring transmission by K slots.

These methods aim to reduce uplink distortion caused by antenna switching.

Cover 0 is a man-to-man defense with no safeties deep to help underneath defenders. It aims to bring maximum blitz pressure, usually by rushing six players, while still covering every eligible receiver. Every non-lineman either covers an offensive player or rushes the quarterback.

**Strengths**
- Assignments are simple and clear.
- Motion is easy to adjust to.
- Adding players to the box helps stop the run.
- It works well against RPOs because coverage players watch their receivers rather than the quarterback.
- Defensive backs have no run responsibilities, so they can break quickly on short routes like hitches and slants. It also helps against screen-heavy teams.
- Rushing six against five offensive linemen shortens the quarterback's time to throw.
- Pre-snap, it can be disguised to look like Cover 4.

**Weaknesses**
- It is high-risk/high-reward. A beaten defender has no help, which can lead to big plays.
- Deep routes can pull defenders away.
- It is vulnerable to draw plays, quarterback scrambles, and pick plays such as the mesh concept.
- As a "middle of the field open" coverage, it leaves the deep middle uncovered. Raiders owner Al Davis forbade it for this reason.

**General rules**
- Cornerbacks cover the X and Z receivers.
- The strong safety covers the tight end, and the free safety covers the slot.
- The Sam linebacker covers the running back.
- The Mike and Will linebackers blitz.

**Variations**
- **"Rat":** rushes five and leaves one free player to take away crossing routes and quarterback runs.
- **Dropping a hybrid defensive lineman into coverage:** the lineman covers a back and can also be used as the "Rat" player.
